programmes.name_en: Jobseeker Support (main unemployment benefit)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Paid weekly; max net rates (at M tax code) from 1 Apr 2026: single 18-19 living with parents $276.46, single 20-24 or 18-19 not with parents $324.50, single 25+ $372.55, couple (total, no children) $633.94, sole parent $521.52. Reduced by income. Full-time students cannot get it (see StudyLink).

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility with the Check What You Might Get tool
Apply online via MyMSD or book an appointment with Work and Income
Attend appointment, provide documents, agree to work obligations

documents_required.doc: Medical certificate (only if work capacity reduced)

eligibility.income_note: Income tested incl. partner's: weekly pre-tax income limits e.g. single 25+ $693, couple no children $1,066, sole parent $957.

programmes.source_snippet: Jobseeker Support is a weekly payment that helps people while they are looking for work or can't work right now.

programmes.name_en: Jobseeker Support Student Hardship (summer break support for students)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment during the break between academic years of a full-time programme; rates in MSD Map (jobseeker-support-student-hardship-current). Apply through StudyLink.
programmes.deadline_note: Applies to the summer study break period each year

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD before the summer break
Provide proof of enrolment for the next year

documents_required.doc: Confirmation of enrolment for next study year

eligibility.income_note: Must have little or no income and be in hardship; available for and seeking full-time work.

programmes.source_snippet: To get Jobseeker Support Student Hardship a client must: ... be a New Zealand citizen or residence class visa holder; have little or no income; be in the break between two academic years of a programme of study

programmes.name_en: Sole Parent Support
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment; max net rate approx $521.52/week from 1 Apr 2026 (per Jobseeker Support page sole-parent rate); see MSD rates table. Only for youngest child under 14.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via MyMSD or contact Work and Income
Attend a work capability interview and provide documents

documents_required.doc: Proof of care of dependent child

eligibility.income_note: Income tested

programmes.source_snippet: Sole Parent Support is a weekly payment that helps single parents find part-time work or get ready for future work.

programmes.name_en: Supported Living Payment
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment for people who have, or care full-time for someone with, a health condition, injury or disability that severely restricts ability to work. Rate depends on age and circumstances.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD or Work and Income appointment
Provide medical certificate from your doctor or specialist

eligibility.income_note: May depend on your and your partner's income; rates and cut-out points published by MSD.

programmes.source_snippet: Supported Living Payment is a weekly payment to help you if you have, or are caring for someone with, a significant health condition, injury or disability.

programmes.name_en: New Zealand Superannuation (universal state pension from age 65)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Fortnightly payment; from 1 Apr 2026 approx $555.15/week net (single living alone, tax code M), $512.45 (single sharing), $427.04 each (qualifying couple). Not income or asset tested.
programmes.deadline_note: Can apply up to 12 weeks before turning 65

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD up to 12 weeks before your 65th birthday
Provide proof of identity and residency history

documents_required.doc: Proof of residence in NZ (10 years since age 20, 5 since age 50)

eligibility.income_note: Not income or asset tested. Residence requirement: 10 to 20 years lived in NZ from age 20 (depending on date of birth; e.g. 12 years for those born 1961-63), including 5 years from age 50.

programmes.source_snippet: You may qualify for NZ Super if you: are 65 or older; either: are a New Zealand (NZ) citizen; are an NZ permanent resident, or hold an NZ residence class visa; are ordinarily resident in New Zealand...

programmes.name_en: Veteran's Pension
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Fortnightly payment at the same rates as NZ Super for qualifying veterans with service-related conditions or aged 65+.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact Work and Income seniors line to apply
Provide service record and medical evidence if under 65

eligibility.income_note: Not income or asset tested

programmes.source_snippet: Veteran's Pension is a fortnightly payment for veterans who have qualifying operational service in the New Zealand Armed Forces.

programmes.name_en: Youth Payment
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment for 16–17 year olds who cannot live with or be supported by their parents and are in education, training or work-based learning.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD with a youth service provider
Enrol in education, training or work-based learning

documents_required.doc: Evidence of circumstances preventing living at home

eligibility.income_note: Parental income may be assessed

programmes.source_snippet: Youth Payment helps young people aged 16 or 17 who can't live with their parents or guardian and aren't supported by them or anyone else.

programmes.name_en: Young Parent Payment
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment for parents aged 16–19 (18–19 with no parental support) whose main role is caring for their child.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD with a youth service provider
Agree a plan for education, training or parenting courses

eligibility.income_note: Income tested

programmes.source_snippet: Young Parent Payment helps young parents aged 16-19 year olds.

programmes.name_en: Emergency Benefit
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly hardship payment for people in hardship who cannot get any other benefit (e.g. residency criteria not yet met).
programmes.deadline_note: Apply by phoning Work and Income on 0800 559 009

procedure_steps.detail: Contact Work and Income to discuss hardship situation
Provide evidence you cannot get any other benefit

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested

programmes.source_snippet: If you can't support yourself and don't qualify for any other payment, you may be able to get the Emergency Benefit.

programmes.name_en: Temporary Additional Support (TAS)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment (max 13 weeks at a time) to cover essential living costs that cannot be met from income and other resources. You do not need to be on a benefit.
programmes.deadline_note: Paid for a maximum of 13 weeks, then reviewed

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD or Work and Income appointment
Provide details of essential costs and income

documents_required.doc: Evidence of accommodation and essential costs

eligibility.income_note: Income, asset and cost tested

programmes.source_snippet: Temporary Additional Support is a weekly payment that helps you when you don't have enough money to cover your essential living costs.

programmes.name_en: Special Benefit (legacy hardship payment)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Legacy weekly hardship payment; largely replaced by Temporary Additional Support since 2007 and now only continued for a small number of existing recipients.
programmes.deadline_note: Legacy payment for existing recipients only; new applicants who need help with essential costs apply for Temporary Additional Support instead

procedure_steps.detail: Contact Work and Income to check what ongoing help you can get

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested

programmes.source_snippet: If you're getting Special Benefit you have to tell us about any income, one-off payments or assets you, or your partner, get.

programmes.name_en: Orphan's Benefit
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment; amount depends on child's age and any income the child has (MSD rates table). Clothing Allowance and $350 Establishment Grant also paid.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD or Work and Income
Provide evidence of the child's circumstances and your care

documents_required.doc: Evidence of parents' death or inability to care

eligibility.income_note: Carer's income not tested for Orphan's Benefit

programmes.source_snippet: Orphan's Benefit is a weekly payment which helps carers supporting a child or young person whose parents have died or can't be found, or can't look after them because they have a serious long-term health condition or incapacity.

programmes.name_en: Unsupported Child's Benefit
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment; amount depends on child's age and any income the child has (MSD rates table). Clothing Allowance and $350 Establishment Grant also paid.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD or Work and Income
Provide evidence the child cannot live with their parents

documents_required.doc: Evidence of family breakdown and care arrangements

eligibility.income_note: Carer's income not tested

programmes.source_snippet: Unsupported Child's Benefit is a weekly payment which helps carers supporting a child or young person whose parents can't care for them because of a family breakdown.

programmes.name_en: Special Needs Grant for food (hardship food grant)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: One-off payment loaded on a payment card (7 days to spend); amount depends on your situation; not repayable; food and essential groceries only. You do not need to be on a benefit.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD urgent costs or call Work and Income
Payment loaded onto a payment card for approved food retailers

eligibility.income_note: Weekly pre-tax income must be under: single 18+ $1,010.41; single 16-17 $879.17; couple $1,467.61; sole parent 1 child $1,226.09; sole parent 2+ children $1,291.75. Also need no cash assets / no other way to pay for food.

programmes.source_snippet: We may be able to help you pay for food if you're on a low income or a benefit. ... are a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident

programmes.name_en: Recoverable Assistance Payment (interest-free hardship loan)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Interest-free, repayable payment for essential immediate needs (e.g. appliances, school costs, car repairs) for people not on a benefit who cannot get an advance. Repaid by instalments.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD urgent costs
Agree a repayment schedule deducted from wages or payments

eligibility.income_note: Annual pre-tax income limits: single 18+ $52,541.32; single 16-17 $45,716.84; couple $76,315.72; sole parent 1 child $63,756.68; 2+ children $67,171. Asset limits: single $1,411.22; couple/sole parent $2,351.46. Figure shown is single 18+.

programmes.source_snippet: A Recoverable Assistance Payment is a one-off payment to help you pay an essential or emergency cost if you can't pay it another way. You don't qualify for this payment if you're on a benefit. You have to pay the money back.

programmes.name_en: Advance Payment of Benefit
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: One-off repayable payment loaded on a payment card (7 days to spend); amount depends on your situation and the cost; repaid from your benefit. The page does not state a 6-week cap.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD or call Work and Income
Provide quote or evidence of the essential cost

documents_required.doc: Quote or invoice for the item

eligibility.income_note: Must be getting a main benefit, Orphan's/Unsupported Child's Benefit, NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Weekly income under $1,010.41 (single 18+); assets under $1,411.22 (single) / $2,351.46 (couple or sole parent).

programmes.source_snippet: An Advance Payment of Benefit is a one-off payment to help you pay an essential or emergency cost if you can't pay it another way. To qualify for this payment you need to be getting a main benefit (e.g., Jobseeker Support), a pension or Orphan's or Unsupported Child's Benefit and you will have...

programmes.name_local: Special Needs Grant — Dental and Glasses
programmes.name_en: Special Needs Grant for emergency dental care and glasses
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Immediate and essential dental treatment: up to $1,000 in any 52-week period, not repayable; more may be possible but may need repaying. Glasses and other health costs are covered by separate Work and Income pages.
programmes.deadline_note: Dental capped at $1,000 per any 52-week period

procedure_steps.detail: Get a quote from the dentist or optometrist
Apply via MyMSD urgent costs

eligibility.income_note: Weekly pre-tax income under $1,010.41 (single 18+), $879.17 (single 16-17), $1,467.61 (couple), $1,226.09 (sole parent 1 child); asset limits $1,411.22 single / $2,351.46 couple or sole parent.

programmes.source_snippet: You can apply for up to $1,000 a year (any 52-week period), to help with immediate and essential dental treatment. You don't have to pay this back.

programmes.name_en: Funeral Grant
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: One-off payment; the most you can be paid is $2,697.43, towards reasonable funeral expenses. Income and asset tested if the deceased is your partner or child; deceased person's assets are deducted. Not repayable if criteria met.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD or Work and Income with the funeral account

documents_required.doc: Death certificate or proof of death

eligibility.income_note: Income limit applies only if the deceased is your partner or child (annual pre-tax e.g. $38,522.12 single 18+ with no children; $55,954.08 couple if the deceased is your child). The deceased must have normally lived in New Zealand.

programmes.source_snippet: A Funeral Grant can help with some of the funeral costs of someone who has died. ... The most you can be paid is $2,697.43.

programmes.name_en: Civil Defence Payment (emergency event support)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Maximum amounts: food/bedding/clothing $400 single to $1,110 (couple/sole parent 3+ children); temporary accommodation up to $1,426/week single; hosted accommodation $261/week single; lost income up to $372.55/week single 25+. No income or asset test in most cases.
programmes.deadline_note: Not currently available (as at 2026-10-05); only made available for a declared emergency event

procedure_steps.detail: Contact Work and Income during a declared emergency event
Provide evidence you were affected by the emergency

documents_required.doc: Proof of address in affected area

eligibility.income_note: Hardship-based, not normally income tested

programmes.source_snippet: Civil Defence Payments are not currently available. ... You don't have to be on a benefit to qualify for a Civil Defence Payment. You also don't have to be a New Zealand resident.

programmes.name_en: ACC weekly compensation (80% income replacement after injury)
programmes.funder: Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC)
programmes.amount_note: Up to 80% of pre-injury weekly earnings if you cannot work because of a covered injury; minimum approx $766.40/week for full-time earners and maximum approx $2,409.86/week (2026/27). Starts from day 8; employer pays first week for work injuries.
programmes.deadline_note: Usually payable from day 8 after your injury

procedure_steps.detail: See a health provider who lodges an ACC claim
Apply for weekly compensation via MyACC or call 0800 101 996
Provide employment and income details

documents_required.doc: ACC claim lodged by treatment provider

eligibility.income_note: Based on pre-injury earnings, not means tested

programmes.source_snippet: We pay up to 80% of your income as weekly compensation if you can't work because of your injury. Get paid while you recover. Apply using MyACC.

programmes.name_local: Working for Families — Family Tax Credit
programmes.name_en: Working for Families Family Tax Credit
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake)
programmes.amount_note: Full amount if family income is $44,900 or less: eldest child $7,921/yr ($152/wk), each other child $6,454/yr ($124/wk). Reduces by 27.5 cents per dollar of family income over $44,900.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via myIR or register when your baby is born via SmartStart
Estimate your family income and confirm details annually

documents_required.doc: IRD numbers for parents and children

eligibility.income_note: Full credit up to $44,900 family income; abates at 27.5% above that, so the cut-off depends on the number of children. Residency: NZ resident for tax, lived in NZ 12 months in a row at any time.

programmes.source_snippet: The family tax credit is the main payment for people who qualify for Working for Families.

programmes.name_local: Working for Families — In-work Tax Credit
programmes.name_en: Working for Families In-work Tax Credit
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake)
programmes.amount_note: From 1 Apr 2026 up to $147/week ($7,670/yr) for 1-3 children, plus $780/yr for each additional child. IRD says this may fall back to $97/week if petrol drops below $3/litre for four weeks, and returns to $97/week ($5,070/yr) after 31 Mar 2027. Not payable on passive income only.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for Working for Families via myIR
Confirm hours of paid work each year

documents_required.doc: IRD numbers for parents and children

eligibility.income_note: Full credit up to $44,900 family income, then abated (27.5%) with any left-over family tax credit abatement. Must be earning income from paid work.

programmes.source_snippet: If you get Working for Families, you'll qualify for an in-work tax credit as long as you're earning income from paid work.

programmes.name_en: Best Start (Working for Families payment for children under 3)
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake)
programmes.amount_note: $77 a week (up to $4,041/yr) for the first 3 years of a child's life. For children born on/after 1 Apr 2026 the payment reduces by 21 cents per dollar of family income over $79,000 in every year; for children born earlier the first year is not income tested.
programmes.deadline_note: Payments stop when the child turns 3

procedure_steps.detail: Register the birth and apply for Best Start via SmartStart
Confirm details with Inland Revenue each year via myIR

documents_required.doc: IRD number for the child (within 8 weeks)

eligibility.income_note: Abates from $79,000 family income at 21%; entitlement reaches nil at about $98,243 (derived: 79,000 + 4,041/0.21). Applies to all years for children born from 1 Apr 2026; years 2-3 for earlier births. Not paid at the same time as paid parental leave.

programmes.source_snippet: Best Start payments give extra support to your family over the 1st 3 years of your child's life. The full entitlement is $77 a week.

programmes.name_en: Working for Families Minimum Family Tax Credit
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake)
programmes.amount_note: Tops net (after-tax) family income up to $36,604/yr ($703/week after tax). Requires minimum paid work hours: single parent 20 hrs/week; couple 30 hrs/week between them. Amount does not depend on number of children.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via myIR with your Working for Families registration
Confirm work hours and income annually

eligibility.income_note: Net (after-tax) family income must be under $36,604 for the year. Not available for self-employed/partnership income alone.

programmes.source_snippet: If you qualify, we'll top up your income so you'll get $703 a week (after tax).

programmes.name_en: Government-funded paid parental leave (up to 26 weeks)
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake)
programmes.amount_note: Higher of ordinary weekly pay and average weekly income, capped at $811.05 gross/week for 1 Jul 2026-30 Jun 2027 ($788.66 for 1 Jul 2025-30 Jun 2026). Same payment regardless of number of children.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before you return to work; payments must be taken in one continuous period

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via myIR before or after the birth
Your employer confirms your leave details
Payments made fortnightly by Inland Revenue

documents_required.doc: Expected due date or birth/adoption details

eligibility.income_note: Must have worked 10+ hrs/week for 26 of the 52 weeks before the due date

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum paid parental leave payment (before tax) is: 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 - $811.05 a week

programmes.name_en: Accommodation Supplement (weekly rent/board/mortgage help)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Weekly, tax-free. Maximum by area and household: Single 16+ $165 (Area 1) to $70 (Area 4); couple with children up to $305 (Area 1) to $120 (Area 4). Must pay above an entry threshold; not payable if living in public housing.
programmes.deadline_note: Reviewed annually by Work and Income

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via MyMSD with proof of accommodation costs
Non-beneficiaries attend a Work and Income appointment
Renew details at each annual review

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested incl. partner; cash assets no more than $8,100 (single) / $16,200 (couple or sole parent).

programmes.source_snippet: Accommodation Supplement is a weekly payment which helps people with their rent, board or the cost of owning a home.

programmes.name_en: Income-Related Rent Subsidy (public/social housing rent at 25% of income)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development / Kāinga Ora / Community Housing Providers
programmes.amount_note: Eligible tenants pay income-related rent based on household income (see Living in public housing); the Government pays the rest.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for the Public Housing Register via Work and Income
MSD assesses eligibility and priority rating
Matched with Kāinga Ora or a community housing provider

eligibility.income_note: Generally income under $832.72/week after tax (single, no children) or $1,281.12/week (partner or children) and cash assets under $42,700; may still qualify above these. Must have a serious housing need.

programmes.source_snippet: Residency: ... you're a New Zealand citizen; you have a resident visa or permanent resident visa and have lived in NZ continuously for at least 2 years since getting it; you're recognised as a refugee ... Age: You must be 16 or older.

programmes.name_en: Emergency Housing Special Needs Grant
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Work and Income generally pays the first 7 nights if you qualify; after that you pay an Emergency Housing Contribution.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact Work and Income when you have nowhere to stay
MSD checks alternative housing options and pays the provider directly

eligibility.income_note: Weekly pre-tax income generally under $740.81 (single 18+), $644.59 (single 16-17), $1,076.04 (couple), $898.96 (sole parent 1 child), $947.09 (2+ children); cash assets under $1,411.22 (single) / $2,351.46 (couple or sole parent).

programmes.source_snippet: If you have nowhere to stay tonight or in the next 7 nights, we may be able to pay for you to stay in emergency housing.

programmes.name_local: Housing Support Products (Bond, Rent in Advance, Rent Arrears, Moving Costs)
programmes.name_en: Housing Support Products — bond, rent in advance, rent arrears and moving cost grants
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Bond Grant: lowest of 4 weeks' rent, the amount the landlord asks, or your share of the bond; it must be repaid (repayment plan). Other moving-house grants (accommodation costs in advance, moving costs, security cover) are on the Moving house page; the earlier '$2,000 non-recoverable' bond figure is not on the official page.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyMSD when starting or retaining a tenancy
Provide tenancy agreement or arrears notice

eligibility.income_note: Weekly pre-tax income under $1,353 (single 16+), $2,006 (couple no children), $2,337 (couple with children), $1,846 (sole parent 1 child); assets under $8,100 single / $16,200 couple or sole parent.

programmes.source_snippet: If you don't have enough money to pay bond to your landlord, you may be able to get a Bond Grant. You'll need to pay the money back.

programmes.name_en: Kāinga Ora First Home Loan (5% deposit, government-underwritten)
programmes.funder: Kāinga Ora — Homes and Communities
programmes.amount_note: Kāinga Ora underwrites a loan from a participating bank so first-home buyers can buy with a 5% deposit. Income caps: $95,000 single (no dependants) / $150,000 single with dependants or combined buyers. No house price cap. A Lender's Mortgage Insurance premium applies.

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility with the Kāinga Ora First Home Decision Tool
Apply through a participating bank or lender with at least 5% deposit

documents_required.doc: Evidence of 5% genuine deposit (can include KiwiSaver)

eligibility.income_note: Before-tax income over last 12 months: $95,000 or less (individual, no dependants); $150,000 or less (individual with dependants); $150,000 or less combined for two or more buyers.

programmes.source_snippet: A First Home Loan can make it easier for you to get into your first home by lowering the required deposit to 5%.

programmes.name_en: KiwiSaver first-home withdrawal
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue / KiwiSaver providers
programmes.amount_note: Withdraw nearly all your KiwiSaver savings (leaving $1,000) to buy your first home, after at least 3 years of membership. No income test. Apply through your KiwiSaver provider before settlement.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply to your KiwiSaver provider before purchase settlement

procedure_steps.detail: Ask your KiwiSaver provider for a first-home withdrawal application
Provide sale and purchase agreement and solicitor details

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested; 3+ years KiwiSaver membership

programmes.source_snippet: If you have been a member of KiwiSaver for at least 3 years, you may be able to make a withdrawal from your savings to put towards buying your first home. ... at least $1,000 must remain in their KiwiSaver account.

programmes.name_en: Kāinga Whenua Loan (build or buy on Māori land)
programmes.funder: Kāinga Ora — Homes and Communities
programmes.amount_note: Loans for Māori to build, purchase or relocate a house on multiply-owned Māori land; also available to Māori land trusts and collectives.

procedure_steps.detail: Discuss your plans with Kāinga Ora
Apply through an approved lender with Kāinga Whenua security arrangements

documents_required.doc: Proof of connection to the whenua/trust
Building or purchase plans and costings

eligibility.income_note: Loan serviceability assessed by lender

programmes.source_snippet: The Kainga Whenua Loan is designed to support whanau Maori with their housing aspirations and remove some of the barriers to accessing finance.

programmes.name_en: Kāinga Ora Tenant Home Ownership Grant
programmes.funder: Kāinga Ora — Homes and Communities
programmes.amount_note: A grant of 10% of the purchase price (up to $20,000) for eligible Kāinga Ora tenants buying the home they live in. Only available for selected Kāinga Ora houses; can be combined with the First Home Loan.
programmes.deadline_note: Only selected Kainga Ora houses; not available in Auckland, Wellington City, Christchurch, Hamilton or Tauranga

procedure_steps.detail: Contact Kāinga Ora to check if your home is eligible
Submit the application and arrange finance

eligibility.income_note: Must be a current Kāinga Ora tenant buying an eligible property

programmes.source_snippet: The Tenant Home Ownership grant is a gift of 10% of the purchase price of selected Kainga Ora houses up to a maximum of $20,000. The Tenant Home Ownership grant is not available in areas where there is high demand for state houses.

programmes.name_en: Rates Rebate Scheme (local council rates relief for low-income homeowners)
programmes.funder: Department of Internal Affairs (administered by local councils)
programmes.amount_note: Maximum rebate $830 for the 2026-27 rating year; must be living in your own home on 1 July 2026. Assessed by your council.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply to your council by 30 June 2027 for the 1 Jul 2026-30 Jun 2027 rating year

procedure_steps.detail: Complete the rates rebate application form for your council
Submit with proof of income and rates to your local council

documents_required.doc: Proof of household income for the previous tax year

eligibility.income_note: Household income up to $33,210 gets the maximum rebate; SuperGold cardholder households up to $46,400. Above these you may still get a smaller rebate (depends on rates paid and dependants). Based on income for 1 Apr 2025-31 Mar 2026.

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum rebate you can get is $830. You may be eligible for all or only part of this amount.

programmes.name_en: Council rates postponement schemes for older or hardship homeowners
programmes.funder: Local councils (e.g. Wellington City Council, Auckland Council)
programmes.amount_note: Council-specific. Example (Wellington City Council): postponement for owner-occupiers in extreme financial hardship as a last resort; approved for one year at a time; $200 application fee; interest charged annually; legal charge over the property. Other councils run their own policies.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your council about their rates postponement policy
Complete the application and agree the postponement charge terms

eligibility.income_note: Criteria vary by council

programmes.source_snippet: The Council may help ratepayers by postponing their rates payments in cases of extreme financial hardship.

programmes.name_en: Community Services Card (subsidised GP visits, prescriptions and transport discounts)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Free card for low-income people: reduced-cost GP visits, free subsidised prescriptions (no $5 charge), and eligibility for the 50% Community Connect public transport concession. Income thresholds depend on household size.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via MyMSD or at a Work and Income service centre
Card posted to you; present it at your GP, pharmacy or transport operator

eligibility.income_note: Yearly pre-tax income limits: single living with others $34,974; single living alone $37,116; couple no children $55,501; family of 2 $67,791; family of 3 $83,444 (NZ Super rates are higher).

programmes.source_snippet: The Community Services Card can help you with the costs of health care and public transport.

programmes.name_en: High Use Health Card (reduced GP fees for frequent users)
programmes.funder: Health New Zealand — Te Whatu Ora (via your GP practice)
programmes.amount_note: Card for people with long-term conditions who have visited their enrolled medical practice 12+ times in a year; reduces GP visit costs and specialist prescription co-payments. Not income tested. Renewed annually.
programmes.deadline_note: Must be reapplied for every year

procedure_steps.detail: Ask your GP practice to apply for a High Use Health Card for you
Use the card when you visit your practice or pharmacy

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested; based on frequency of GP visits

programmes.source_snippet: You may be eligible for a High Use Health Card if you have visited a healthcare practitioner at the general practice you are enrolled in 12 or more times in one year. The 12 visits must be related to a health condition that is ongoing, and not be related to an injury.

programmes.name_local: Prescription Charge and Prescription Subsidy Card
programmes.name_en: $5 prescription co-payment with exemptions, and free prescriptions after 20 items (Prescription Subsidy Card)
programmes.funder: Health New Zealand — Te Whatu Ora / Pharmac
programmes.amount_note: Standard $5 charge per subsidised medicine on new prescriptions. FREE for under-14s, 65+, Community Services Card and Prescription Subsidy Card holders. After 20 paid items per family from 1 February, the PSC makes further items free until 31 January.
programmes.deadline_note: PSC year runs 1 February to 31 January

procedure_steps.detail: Pay the $5 charge at the pharmacy for new prescriptions (unless exempt)
Tell your pharmacist your family members so items count towards the 20-item threshold
After 20 items the Prescription Subsidy Card is issued automatically

eligibility.income_note: Exemptions for under-14, 65+, CSC and PSC holders

programmes.source_snippet: People need to pay the standard $5 prescription charge, with exemptions for people: aged 13 years or under; holding a Community Services Card (CSC), or a dependent child of a CSC holder; aged 65 years or over; holding a Prescription Subsidy Card (PSC).

programmes.name_en: Disability Allowance (weekly help with ongoing disability costs)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Up to $82.85 a week depending on your extra disability costs; not taxed and not repayable.

procedure_steps.detail: Get your doctor to complete the Disability Certificate
Apply via MyMSD with receipts or evidence of costs

documents_required.doc: Disability Certificate from a health practitioner

eligibility.income_note: Weekly pre-tax income limits: single 18+ $870; single 16-17 $696.60; couple $1,295.11; sole parent 1 child $971.51; 2+ children $1,023.59.

programmes.source_snippet: Disability Allowance is a weekly payment for people who have regular, ongoing costs because of a disability.

programmes.name_en: Child Disability Allowance
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Fixed $62.43 a week per qualifying child, paid fortnightly; not affected by income, assets or costs.

procedure_steps.detail: Get your doctor or specialist to complete the medical section
Apply via MyMSD or Work and Income

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested

programmes.source_snippet: Child Disability Allowance is a fortnightly payment made to the main carer of a child or young person with a serious disability.

programmes.name_en: Free breast screening (mammogram) for women 45–69
programmes.funder: Health New Zealand — National Screening Unit
programmes.amount_note: Free mammograms for eligible women aged 45 to 69, or 70 to 74 if they qualify for the screening age extension. For most women every 2 years (for 70-74 it depends on birth date). Not for people ineligible for publicly funded health care.
programmes.deadline_note: Screening recommended every 2 years

procedure_steps.detail: Call 0800 270 200 or enrol via your GP
Attend a screening centre or mobile unit

eligibility.income_note: Free; not income tested

programmes.source_snippet: Eligible women (those aged between 45 and 69 or those who qualify for the age range extension for women aged 70 to 74) can get regular free mammograms.

programmes.name_en: Free/subsidised cervical screening (HPV test)
programmes.funder: Health New Zealand — National Screening Unit
programmes.amount_note: The programme is not fully funded. Free routine screening if: Maori or Pacific aged 25-69; aged 25-69 with a Community Services Card; aged 30+ and never screened or overdue (5+ years since last cytology / 7+ since last HPV test); aged 70-74 and never screened or without recent normal results. Follow-up tests free for all. People not eligible for publicly funded health care pay for everything.
programmes.deadline_note: Screening every 3 years (or 5 years for HPV-negative self-test)

procedure_steps.detail: Book a screening test or request an HPV self-test at your GP or clinic

eligibility.income_note: Free only for priority groups (Maori/Pacific, Community Services Card holders, never/under-screened); not otherwise free

programmes.source_snippet: The National Cervical Screening Programme is not fully funded. Free routine cervical screening ... is available if you are: ... Māori and Pacific wāhine aged 25 to 69 years; aged 25 to 69 and hold a Community Services Card.

programmes.name_en: Free bowel screening test for ages 58–74
programmes.funder: Health New Zealand — National Screening Unit
programmes.amount_note: Free home test kit mailed every 2 years to people aged 58 to 74 (from 56 in Waitemata, Auckland, Counties Manukau, Waikato, Tairawhiti, Wairarapa, West Coast and South Canterbury districts; other districts expected to move to 56 in early 2027). No need to apply. Free for people eligible for publicly funded health care.
programmes.deadline_note: Kit sent automatically around your birthday every 2 years

procedure_steps.detail: Complete and return the free test kit when it arrives in the post

documents_required.doc: None — kit posted to enrolled people

eligibility.income_note: Free; not income tested

programmes.source_snippet: People eligible for publicly funded health care can have free bowel screening through the programme.

programmes.name_en: Free GP visits and after-hours care for children under 14
programmes.funder: Health New Zealand — Te Whatu Ora
programmes.amount_note: Children under 14 enrolled with a general practice get free daytime GP visits and free after-hours care at participating clinics.

procedure_steps.detail: Enrol your child with a general practice
Visits are free at the enrolled practice and participating after-hours clinics

documents_required.doc: Child enrolled with a general practice

eligibility.income_note: Free; not income tested

programmes.source_snippet: All tamariki aged 13 and under who are eligible for publicly funded health services, are eligible for free doctor visits and more.

programmes.name_local: ACC Treatment, Rehabilitation and Social Support
programmes.name_en: ACC-funded treatment, attendant care, home help and home modifications after injury
programmes.funder: Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC)
programmes.amount_note: ACC pays part or all of covered treatment costs (GP, physio, surgery), plus rehabilitation support such as attendant care, home help, childcare help, transport to appointments, vocational rehabilitation, and home or vehicle modifications after serious injury.

procedure_steps.detail: Your treatment provider lodges an ACC claim when you are injured
ACC confirms cover and arranges treatment and support entitlements

documents_required.doc: Assessment by ACC for social/vocational support

eligibility.income_note: Not means tested; covers everyone in NZ including visitors

programmes.source_snippet: Along with financial support if you can't work or have a permanent injury, we can pay for things like transport to get you to appointments or work, childcare and help around the home.

programmes.name_en: Funded home help hours for families with twins or triplets
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: 240 hours of funded home help for twins with an older sibling under 5, and 1,560 hours for triplets or more, paid at a maximum hourly rate (about $26.72). Use within 12 months (twins) or 24 months (triplets+).
programmes.deadline_note: Hours must be used within 12 or 24 months of the birth

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through Work and Income after the birth
Arrange and pay your home helper, then claim reimbursement

documents_required.doc: Birth certificates for the multiple-birth children

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested

programmes.source_snippet: If a client has given birth or adopted twins, they can only get Home Help for multiple births if they also have another child who is under the age of 5 years old.

programmes.name_en: Community Connect — 50% off public transport for Community Services Card holders
programmes.funder: NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi / regional councils (AT, Metlink, Metro)
programmes.amount_note: 50% discount on adult public transport fares for Community Services Card holders, applied to a registered AT HOP (Auckland), Snapper (Wellington Metlink) or Metrocard (Canterbury). Free HOP/Metrocard when applying.
programmes.deadline_note: Concession expires when the Community Services Card expires

procedure_steps.detail: Get a Community Services Card from Work and Income
Apply the concession to your registered AT HOP / Snapper / Metrocard online
Carry your CSC when travelling

documents_required.doc: Current Community Services Card (MSD client number)
Registered AT HOP, Snapper or Metrocard

eligibility.income_note: Must hold a Community Services Card (income tested)

programmes.source_snippet: This gives you a 50% discount on most buses, trains and ferries.

programmes.name_en: SuperGold Card — free off-peak public transport plus thousands of discounts
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development
programmes.amount_note: Free concession card issued automatically with NZ Super or Veteran's Pension: free off-peak travel on scheduled buses, trains and ferries nationwide (weekdays after 9am, all weekend and public holidays) plus discounts at 2,800+ businesses.

procedure_steps.detail: Card is mailed automatically once NZ Super or Veteran's Pension is granted
Show the card for off-peak transport and business discounts, or load the concession on a gold AT HOP card

documents_required.doc: None — issued automatically with NZ Super/Veteran's Pension

eligibility.income_note: No income test; Veteran's Pension holders qualify under 65

programmes.source_snippet: Use your SuperGold card or Veteran SuperGold card to get business discounts, free or discounted council services, and free off-peak travel on public transport.

programmes.name_en: Total Mobility Scheme (subsidised taxi transport for people with impairments)
programmes.funder: NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi / regional councils
programmes.amount_note: Subsidy of 65% of each taxi/ride fare (from 1 July 2026) up to a maximum subsidy per trip; you pay the rest. Eligibility is by a mobility assessment for people with permanent disabilities or long-term impairments. Run by regional transport authorities.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your regional council to arrange an eligibility assessment
Receive your Total Mobility card or vouchers and book with approved operators

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested; based on mobility impairment

programmes.source_snippet: The subsidy per trip is 65% of the fare, (from 1 July 2026) up to a maximum subsidy.

programmes.name_en: Auckland Transport tertiary student fare concession
programmes.funder: Auckland Transport
programmes.amount_note: 40% discount on most Auckland buses, trains and ferries for full-time students at Auckland tertiary institutions registered with Auckland Transport (not Waiheke/Rakino ferries or other regions). Loaded on a registered AT HOP card.
programmes.deadline_note: Concession expires after 3 years (UoA, AUT, Massey online applications) or at the earliest of 31 March next year, sticker expiry or student ID expiry (other institutions)

procedure_steps.detail: Register your AT HOP card and apply for the tertiary concession online
Your institution confirms your enrolment to AT

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested

programmes.source_snippet: Full-time students at Auckland tertiary institutions can get a 40% discount on most buses, trains and ferries.

programmes.name_en: Winter Energy Payment (automatic winter top-up for beneficiaries and superannuitants)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Automatic weekly payment 1 May–1 October: $20.46/week single without dependent children; $31.82/week for couples and people with dependent children (approx $450/$700 over the 22-week season). Non-taxable; paid with main benefits, NZ Super and Veteran's Pension.
programmes.deadline_note: Paid automatically 1 May to 1 October each year

procedure_steps.detail: No application needed — paid automatically with your qualifying benefit or pension

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested; tied to receipt of a qualifying benefit, NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

programmes.source_snippet: If you are a single person with no dependent children, you'll receive $20.46 per week. For couples and people with dependent children, you'll receive $31.82 per week.

programmes.name_en: Warmer Kiwi Homes — insulation and heat pump grants
programmes.funder: Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority (EECA)
programmes.amount_note: Grant covering 50–90% of ceiling and underfloor insulation costs, and 90% (up to $3,450) of an approved high-wall heat pump. For owner-occupied homes built before 2008 with a Community Services Card, SuperGold Combo card, or in an eligible low-to-middle-income area. Wood/pellet burner grants ended January 2026.
programmes.deadline_note: Programme funding confirmed to 30 June 2027

procedure_steps.detail: Check your address with the EECA eligibility tool or call 0800 749 782
An EECA-approved service provider quotes with the grant deducted
Pay only the non-funded portion directly to the installer

documents_required.doc: Proof of home ownership and occupancy
Community Services Card or SuperGold Combo card (if applicable)

eligibility.income_note: Targeted to CSC holders and low-to-middle-income areas; home must be built before 2008

programmes.source_snippet: You may be able to get a 90% grant (up to $3,450) if you have a Community Services Card, SuperGold Combo card, or live in the highest-need areas.

programmes.name_en: Childcare Subsidy (income-tested help with pre-school childcare fees)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Up to $6.72 per child per hour (maximum rate, lower incomes) - $336 per week for 50 hours. Normally up to 9 hours a week if not working/studying, up to 50 hours if working, studying, training or in other listed situations. Paid to the childcare provider.

procedure_steps.detail: Enrol your child with a licensed ECE provider
Apply via MyMSD with income and care details

documents_required.doc: Evidence of income and work/study hours

eligibility.income_note: Weekly gross household income test at 1 April 2026: subsidy cuts out at $2,404/week (1 child), $2,748 (2 children), $3,091 (3+ children). Annual figure is the 3+ children cut-out ($3,091 x 52); 1 child = about $125,008, 2 children = about $142,896.

programmes.source_snippet: you're a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident | your family is on a low or middle income.

programmes.name_en: OSCAR Subsidy (out-of-school care and recreation for children 5–13)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Up to $6.72 per child per hour: up to $134.40 a week in term time (20 hours) and $336 a week in school holidays (50 hours). Child must be at school and under 14 (under 18 with Child Disability Allowance). Caregiver must be working, studying/training or in another listed situation. Paid to the provider.

procedure_steps.detail: Enrol your child with an OSCAR-approved programme
Apply via MyMSD with income and care details

documents_required.doc: Evidence of income and work/study hours

eligibility.income_note: Same weekly gross income tables as Childcare Subsidy (1 April 2026): cut-out $2,404/week (1 child), $2,748 (2), $3,091 (3+). Annual figure = 3+ children cut-out x 52; 1 child about $125,008.

programmes.source_snippet: OSCAR Subsidy helps with the cost of before-school, after-school and school holiday programmes for children aged 5 to 13.

programmes.name_en: 20 Hours Early Childhood Education (free ECE for 3–5 year olds)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Education
programmes.amount_note: Up to 20 hours of early childhood education per week (max 6 hours a day) for 3, 4 and 5 year olds; you cannot be charged fees for those hours. Optional charges and hours beyond 20 may be charged. Some services may not offer it.
programmes.deadline_note: From third birthday until starting school

procedure_steps.detail: Enrol your child at a licensed ECE service offering 20 Hours ECE
Attest on the enrolment form which hours are claimed as 20 Hours ECE

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested

programmes.source_snippet: If a child is 3, 4 or 5, they are eligible for the 20 hours ECE funding scheme. The subsidy covers up to 20 hours of early childhood education each week. It can only be used for up to 6 hours a day.

programmes.name_en: Fees Free — final year of first tertiary qualification fees paid back
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue (with Tertiary Education Commission)
programmes.amount_note: Pays back up to $12,000 of fees for the FINAL year of your first eligible tertiary qualification (or final 2 years of work-based learning) after you complete. Applies to final years started on/after 1 Jan 2025; scheme finishes end of 2026. Paid to your student loan balance or bank account via myIR.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply within 12 months of completing an eligible qualification; scheme ends for completions after 31 December 2026

procedure_steps.detail: Complete and pass your first eligible qualification or work-based programme
Apply for your Fees Free entitlement in myIR
Entitlement is paid to your student loan or nominated bank account

documents_required.doc: Completed qualification confirmed by your provider

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested; prior-study and residency criteria apply

programmes.source_snippet: Fees Free covers fees for the final year of tertiary study or final 2 years of work-based learning... up to $12,000. The Government has announced it is ending Fees Free at the end of 2026.

programmes.name_en: Student Allowance (weekly living support for full-time students)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — StudyLink
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment for full-time students that does not have to be paid back. Income tested (personal, and parental income if under 24 without children). Not paid over the summer break.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before 16 December for the following study year

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via StudyLink (MyStudyLink)
Provide enrolment confirmation and income/parental income details

documents_required.doc: Income details (and parental income if under 24)

eligibility.income_note: No single-person ceiling is published. For a student without a partner, personal income above $284.70 a week before tax reduces the allowance cent for cent, so the cut-out depends on the applicable weekly rate. StudyLink does publish a partnered cut-out: combined income of $1,185.75 a week before tax ($61,659 a year) means you cannot get a Student Allowance. Rates valid from 31 March 2026.

programmes.source_snippet: A Student Allowance is a weekly payment that can help with your living expenses while you’re studying. ... In most cases you have to be: between 18-65, and studying full-time.

programmes.name_en: Student Loan living costs component (in-kind loan, repayable)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — StudyLink / Inland Revenue
programmes.amount_note: Living-costs loan of up to $333.48 a week for full-time students (not available if you are on a benefit or in prison). Repayable. If you are 55 or older you can only borrow compulsory course fees, so no living costs. Reduced by any Student Allowance.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before your course starts each year

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyStudyLink as part of your student loan application
Choose the living costs amount (reduces if you get a Student Allowance)

eligibility.income_note: Not means tested but reduced by any Student Allowance received

programmes.source_snippet: A Student Loan can help pay for your course fees, study materials and living costs — you have to pay it back.

programmes.name_en: Student Loan course-related costs (up to $1,000/year)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — StudyLink / Inland Revenue
programmes.amount_note: Up to $1,000 per year loan component for course-related costs (books, equipment, materials), repayable through the student loan system.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before your course starts each year

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via MyStudyLink as part of your student loan
Claim actual course-related expenses up to the $1,000 limit

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested

programmes.source_snippet: You can borrow up to $1,000 a year for course-related costs such as textbooks and equipment.

programmes.name_en: Training Incentive Allowance (course costs help for people on certain benefits)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: $143.08 for each week of study, up to $5,723.20 in a 52-week period. Paid weekly, upfront for costs such as fees or a laptop, or a mix. For people on Sole Parent Support, Supported Living Payment, Young Parent Payment (sole parents), Emergency Benefit/EMA (sole parents) or Jobseeker Support (sole parents) studying an approved course of 12+ weeks at levels 1-7.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply within 28 days of your study starting; reapply each year or for a new course

procedure_steps.detail: Discuss your study plan with Work and Income
Apply via MyMSD with course fee details

documents_required.doc: Proof of enrolment and course fees

eligibility.income_note: Must be receiving a qualifying benefit

programmes.source_snippet: Training Incentive Allowance helps with the costs of studying an approved course while on certain benefits.

programmes.name_en: School donations scheme (schools with Equity Index 432+ can opt in; parents not asked for donations)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Education
programmes.amount_note: Paid to the school, not to families: eligible state and state-integrated schools and kura with an Equity Index (EQI) of 432 or higher can opt in and receive a per-student rate (see MoE operational funding rates) if they agree not to ask parents for donations (except overnight camps). Families at opted-in schools are not asked for donations.
programmes.deadline_note: School boards opt in each year via the July roll return or a late opt-in form by late November

procedure_steps.detail: Check with your school whether it has opted into the donations scheme
If opted in, the school cannot ask you for donations (camps excepted)

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested; depends on school opting in

programmes.source_snippet: State and state-integrated schools and kura with an equity index (EQI) of 432 or higher can choose to join the scheme. To join, schools and kura must agree not to ask parents and caregivers for donations (except for overnight camps).

programmes.name_local: Ka Ora, Ka Ako — Healthy School Lunches Programme
programmes.name_en: Free school lunches for students at participating high-need schools
programmes.funder: Ministry of Education
programmes.amount_note: Free healthy lunch every school day for students at participating schools and kura, chosen using the Equity Index; more than 240,000 students are served. Not income tested for families.
programmes.deadline_note: Available only at participating schools; programme currently funded for 2025, 2026 and 2027

procedure_steps.detail: Enrol at a participating school — lunches are provided automatically each school day

eligibility.income_note: School-level targeting by equity index, not family income

programmes.source_snippet: We provide healthy lunches every school day to more than 240,000 students who need them to support their learning and thrive.

programmes.name_local: Ikura | Free Period Products in Schools
programmes.name_en: Free period products (pads and tampons) available in all state and state-integrated schools
programmes.funder: Ministry of Education
programmes.amount_note: Free period products (pads and tampons) available in most state and state-integrated primary, intermediate and secondary schools and kura; students can ask at school.
programmes.deadline_note: Schools opt in to receive funded products

procedure_steps.detail: Products are available free at your school — ask the school office or nurse

eligibility.income_note: Not income tested

programmes.source_snippet: We provide free period products in schools and kura across New Zealand so students can learn, participate and stay engaged in school without barriers.

programmes.name_en: Flexi-wage (wage subsidy for hiring people at risk of long-term unemployment)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Wage contribution paid to the employer: $5,638.68 (GST inclusive) in total over 24 weeks, or $11,277.36 (GST inclusive) over 36 weeks, depending on the support the person needs; plus training and ongoing support. Employer must pay at least the adult minimum wage and contact Work and Income before the person starts. A separate Flexi-wage for self-employment exists.

procedure_steps.detail: Talk to Work and Income about a Flexi-wage for a new hire or self-employment
Agree the subsidy terms before the job or business starts

documents_required.doc: IRD and GST details for employers

eligibility.income_note: For jobseekers at risk of long-term unemployment

programmes.source_snippet: Flexi-wage helps you hire staff and get them the skills needed to do the job. You get a wage contribution, while they get training and ongoing support.

programmes.name_en: Self-Employment Start-up Payment (business start-up help for jobseekers)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Amount depends on your situation. Can pay for equipment, initial start-up stock, materials, premises renovation, connection fees, first month's lease/bond, legal, insurance, marketing and a basic website.

procedure_steps.detail: Present your business plan to Work and Income
Apply before incurring start-up costs

eligibility.income_note: Must be out of work, disadvantaged in the labour market and at risk of long-term benefit dependency (usually getting or qualifying for a benefit); business plan must be assessed as viable

programmes.source_snippet: If you're starting a business and need help with essential start up costs, eg furniture or the first lot of stock, we may be able to help.

programmes.name_en: Apprenticeship Boost ($500/month payment to employers of first-year apprentices)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income (with Tertiary Education Commission)
programmes.amount_note: $500 per month (excl GST) paid directly to employers for up to 12 months per apprentice training in a targeted occupation, while in their first 12 months of training. Employer must pay at least the minimum or training wage.
programmes.deadline_note: Up to 12 months of support per eligible apprentice

procedure_steps.detail: Employer creates an account and applies via Work and Income
Reconfirm eligibility each month to keep receiving payments

documents_required.doc: Apprentice training agreement details (verified with TEC)

eligibility.income_note: Apprentice must be in a targeted occupation and first 12 months of training

programmes.source_snippet: From 1 January 2025, employers can receive up to 12 months of support per eligible apprentice. Payments are currently $500 per month (excluding GST).

programmes.name_local: Mana in Mahi — Strength in Work
programmes.name_en: Mana in Mahi (wage subsidy plus industry training for jobseekers)
programmes.funder: Ministry of Social Development — Work and Income
programmes.amount_note: Employer wage subsidy of up to $16,000 paid for 1 year (pro-rated for part-time), up to $2,000 for pre-employment training and up to $8,000 towards industry training fees; the employee can get incentive payments of up to $3,000 over 1 year. Employer must offer a permanent job at at least the adult minimum wage with an NZQA-approved training pathway.

procedure_steps.detail: Register interest with Work and Income as an employer or jobseeker
Agree the subsidy and training plan before employment starts

eligibility.income_note: For jobseekers referred by Work and Income

programmes.source_snippet: a wage subsidy of up to $16,000 paid for 1 year (pro-rated if the employee is working part-time)

programmes.name_en: Independent Earner Tax Credit
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake)
programmes.amount_note: Tax credit of up to $520 a year ($10/week) for people earning between $24,000 and $70,000 who are not receiving Working for Families, a main benefit, NZ Super or Veteran's Pension. Claimed via the ME tax code or at year end.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed through your tax code or end-of-year assessment

procedure_steps.detail: Use the ME or ME SL tax code with your employer
Or claim at the end of the tax year via myIR

eligibility.income_note: For annual incomes $24,000–$70,000 (abates from $44,000); cannot be received with Working for Families, a main benefit, NZ Super or Veteran's Pension

programmes.source_snippet: If you're using a ME or ME SL tax code you'll need to change this with your employer when you apply for Working for Families — you cannot receive both (IR201).

programmes.name_en: KiwiSaver annual government contribution
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake)
programmes.amount_note: Government contributes 25 cents per dollar you contribute, up to $260.72 a year (you must contribute at least $1,042.86 between 1 July and 30 June to get the maximum). Paid via your KiwiSaver provider; no claim needed.
programmes.deadline_note: Paid annually after the KiwiSaver year ends 30 June

procedure_steps.detail: Contribute at least $1,042.86 during the year to get the maximum
Government contribution is paid automatically into your KiwiSaver account

eligibility.income_note: Individual taxable income of $180,000 or under per year; must contribute to KiwiSaver ($1,042.86 between 1 July and 30 June for the full amount)

programmes.source_snippet: If you’re contributing to KiwiSaver, the government will contribute up to $260.72 each year. To get it all you must have contributed at least $1042.86 in the period 1 July to 30 June.

programmes.name_en: R&D Tax Incentive — 15% tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure
programmes.funder: Inland Revenue and Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
programmes.amount_note: 15% tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure between $50,000 and $120 million per year (lower spend possible via an Approved Research Provider). Jointly administered by IRD and MBIE; in-year payments introduced from Budget 2026.
programmes.deadline_note: General Approval required by the last day of the 3rd month after year end; supplementary return within 30 days of tax return due date

procedure_steps.detail: Enrol via myIR and assess eligibility
